name: North Carolina
summary: Statutes, constitution, Rules of Civil Procedure (G.S. 1A-1) and Rules of Evidence (G.S. 8C-1): ncleg.gov per-section and per-rule URLs are constructible from the citation and readable by WebFetch and fetch_doc.py; the site says the text is 'Not Official'. Appellate, General Practice and Business Court rules are single codified PDFs on nccourts.gov, which refuses the script (CloudFront 403); WebFetch reads the rules pages. Case law: appellate.nccourts.org year listings, headnote search and docket sheets work by plain GET, but robots.txt disallows the opinion PDFs under /opinions/, so text comes from Justia (tier 2) and official page numbers from the nccourts.gov N.C./N.C. App. volume PDFs. PDR dispositions are on Supreme Court docket sheets and order PDFs. The NCAC is http-only at reports.oah.state.nc.us (the script's https robots check fails); LII mirrors it but lags.

citation_map.notes: Order matters: try the 1A-1 and 8C-1 rule patterns before the General Statutes pattern, because 'N.C.G.S. § 1A-1, Rule 12' also matches the statute regex as § 1A-1 (a stub page). The statute URL needs no code key: chapter and section come straight from 'G.S. {chapter}-{section}'; law_aliases maps rule-set and act names to their chapter. 'G.S.' is guarded by requiring the dotted form 'G.S.'; bare 'Rule 12', 'Rules of Civil Procedure' or 'Rules of Evidence' route here only with 'North Carolina'/'N.C.' or 1A-1/8C-1 context. 'S.L. YYYY-N' is also used by other states (e.g. Idaho), so route session laws here only with N.C. context. NC sections are always chapter-hyphen-section, so '§§ 1-52 to 1-56' is a span: take the first; '§§ 7B-903, -906.1' gives 7B-903 then 7B-906.1. Official reporters N.C. and N.C. App. are free as whole-volume PDFs on nccourts.gov (nc-reports-volumes); S.E.2d/S.E.3d are West. Universal citations ('2021-NCSC-1', '2021-NCCOA-1', ¶ pinpoints) were a parallel cite for opinions filed from Jan. 1, 2021; the Supreme Court withdrew the order on Jan. 11, 2023. Business Court 'YYYY NCBC N' is a court-assigned public-domain cite. Unpublished COA opinions (N.C. R. App. P. 30(e)) are cited by docket 'No. COA##-###' plus date and '(unpublished)'. Supreme docket suffixes: A (appeal of right), PA (PDR allowed), P (petition), -2 for a second matter. 'disc. review denied, ___ N.C. ___' is found on the Supreme Court docket sheet (nc-subsequent-history-dockets). CourtListener ids from memory, unverified (Business Court opinions may sit under ncsuperct). Westlaw cites with a '(N.C. Super. Ct.' parenthetical (and NCBC LEXIS) are Business Court decisions: they route to nc-business-court-opinions; the general WL pattern excludes them with a negative lookahead (?!\s*Super). Reported-case text routes to Justia first, because the official volume PDFs have not been read. 'G.S.' must not be preceded by a letter or period (Connecticut's 'C.G.S.'); 'section N-N of the General Statutes' is also Connecticut usage, so that bare form routes here only once North Carolina is established.

sources.title: North Carolina General Statutes (ncleg.gov)
sources.official_status_evidence: https://www.ncleg.gov/Laws/GeneralStatutes has a heading 'Not Official': the General Assembly is not responsible for errors or omissions; editor's notes are only in print or LexisNexis.
sources.coverage: All chapters of the General Statutes, per section (HTML, PDF, RTF), per article and per chapter.

access.pattern_rules: Citation G.S. {chapter}-{section}: chapter = everything before the hyphen, with its letter suffix kept (1, 1A, 14, 15A, 75, 143B, 160D); section = everything after the hyphen, decimals verbatim (75-1.1 → GS_75-1.1, 143B-135.40 → GS_143B-135.40). No zero-padding. Path case does not matter (search engines index lower-case copies). Same path with /PDF/ and .pdf, or /RTF/ and .rtf. Whole chapter: /EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/ByChapter/Chapter_{chapter}.html (and /PDF/ByChapter/Chapter_{chapter}.pdf); whole article: /HTML/ByArticle/Chapter_{chapter}/Article_{article}.html. The Rules of Civil Procedure (G.S. 1A-1) and Rules of Evidence (G.S. 8C-1) are single sections whose rules sit in separate files: GS_1A-1,_Rule_{rule}.html and GS_8C-1,_Rule_{rule}.html (see nc-rules-civil-ncleg, nc-rules-evidence-ncleg). Section listing per chapter: https://www.ncleg.gov/Laws/GeneralStatuteSections/Chapter{chapter} (links only, no ranges needed since the URL is direct).

automation.robots_txt: User-agent * — Disallow /WHPTest/, /Ethics/; Crawl-delay: 2
automation.notes: Per-section pages are small (G.S. 1-52: 5,444 chars). Chapter-level files are long: Chapter_1A.html is 301,629 chars of HTML (WebFetch reports 131,823 chars of text and stops inside Rule 20; Rule 56(c) NOT PRESENT). Use the per-section/per-rule file, or fetch_doc.py on the chapter file. WebFetch on ncleg.gov URLs only worked for URLs that a web search had returned (provenance gate in this harness).

sources.coverage: Supreme Court dockets (PDRs, appeals of right, Business Court appeals) with rulings and dates, lower-court numbers, and order PDFs.

access.pattern_rules: Plain GET. court=1 Supreme, court=2 COA. docket = Supreme docket (353PA23) or COA docket (23-305); title = substring of the caption. Result rows link to the sheet https://appellate.nccourts.org/dockets.php?court=1&docket={internal e.g. 1-2023-0353-001}&pdf=1&a=0&dev=1, which lists each motion/PDR with ruling and date ('(1) PDR … Allowed 05-21-2024'), the COA and trial-court numbers, opinion date and decision ('Modified and Affirmed'). Orders: https://appellate.nccourts.org/orders.php?court=1&docket={docket}&title=&submit=Search → order PDFs at orders.php?t=PA&court=1&id={id}&pdf=1&a=0&docket=1&dev=1.
